2 · Resolve unmapped codes

Sites send local codes. Each must resolve to a WHONET code before it can enter the submission. Resolutions persist, so a code is mapped once and not again.
⚠️
14 unmapped codes across 2 sites. Records carrying them are held out of the submission — they are not dropped, and they re-enter automatically once mapped.
Local codeSiteKindRecordsSuggested WHONET code
E_COLI_ESBLInstitut Pasteur CIOrganism412eco — Escherichia coli

URINE_MIInstitut Pasteur CISpecimen1,204no suggestion
Suggestions are proposals shown for a human to accept — never auto-applied. A wrong organism mapping silently corrupts a national resistance rate.

3 · De-duplication & scope

First-isolate selection runs here, at national level — not at each site. Sites send every consecutive isolate; this is the only layer that can see a patient tested at two facilities.

5 · Upload to WHO GLASS

This step is not automated and will not be.
✔️
The nominated focal point downloads both files and uploads them at glass.who.int. GLASS platform credentials are issued to a named individual and cannot be shared or used by a system.
Focal pointNominated byLast submissionPeriod
Dr A. BambaMinistry of Health2025-06-30Jan–Dec 2024
“Record a submission” logs date, period and who uploaded — so the next revision cycle knows what was already sent.
Scope note — this console is the submission surface: periodic, WHO-format, produced for a human to upload. Continuous programme views live under AMR dashboards and have no WHO format constraints. A country can have excellent dashboards and still be unable to submit; the two must not be conflated.
